ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. I re-read it before every fix round. It decides who fixes this round (resume the implementer or dispatch fresh), how the re-review runs, and the five-attempt cap.

ACTION: Dispatch a fix subagent for Task 4, model `sonnet` (resumed or fresh, whichever fix-loop.md says for round 1). The prompt carries finding F1 verbatim: `fetch/retry.py:41` uses `attempt > max_retries` where it should be `attempt >= max_retries`, which makes one extra retry. It also asks for a test in `tests/test_retry.py` that asserts the exact retry count, written so it fails on the old code and passes on the fix. It points to the task brief and the global constraints, and asks for a commit and a report.

ACTION: When the fix commits, generate a new review package with `scripts/review-package` and dispatch the scoped re-review (`re-review-prompt.md`). It gives a per-finding ADDRESSED / NOT ADDRESSED verdict on F1 and checks for new Critical/Important issues.

ACTION: When the re-review is clean, append the Task 4 `complete` line to `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/progress.md` and continue to Task 5.

Message to partner:

I'm sending F1 (the off-by-one in `fetch/retry.py:41`) to a fix subagent instead of editing it myself, even though it's a one-character change. The skill lets me hand-fix only wording or typo changes that don't alter behavior. Changing `>` to `>=` changes how many retries the client makes, so it goes to a subagent. I know you asked me to fix tiny things myself, so I'm flagging that I'm not following that here.

Hand-fixing would also leave the bug uncovered. `tests/test_retry.py` only checks that a retry happens, not how many, so the fix subagent will add a test that pins the exact count and fails on the current code.

After the fix I'll run a scoped re-review of F1, then move on to Task 5.
